---README---
﻿![Logo](logologo.png)
# Tekno FM-1 Jiant Rework

> **A small patch for JIANT FM** — six techno-family genres replacing generic world/jazz/hip-hop slots.

**Based on**: [JIANT FM](https://github.com/juanjiant-bit/JIANT) v0.9.18  
**Patch by**: MarcoCasanova00  
**Original authors**: Juan Jiant (Juan Ignacio Antonucci), Hügelton Instruments (Felucca)

## What Changed (Replaced)
| Removed (original) | Replaced with |
|--------------------|---------------|
| BROKEN | PSY TRANCE |
| AFROBEAT | TEKNO |
| BOSSA | MENTAL TEKNO |
| JAZZ | ACID CORE |
| BOOM BAP | HARDTEKK |
| STEPPERS | TRIBE TEKNO |

All original 43-genre count preserved — each new genre occupies a slot vacated by the removed ones. PSY TRANCE sits in the old BROKEN slot (42), so genre indices 0–42 remain stable.

- **11 new generator recipes** tuned for techno tempos, kick/bass interaction, accent displacement, and polymeter
- **8 new playable ANALOG presets**: TRIBE BASS, TEKK BASS, PSY BASS, CORE 303, TEKK STAB, PSY LEAD, TEKNO BASS, MENTAL RING
- **6 new drum maps** with genre-specific kick patterns, hi-hats, percussion
- **6 new bass archetypes** designed against the new kick rules

### Generator core (second pass)
The dedicated tekno recipes now keep their own envelopes instead of being overwritten by role defaults, the six rows use four distinct kick/bass handovers, and a deterministic articulation pass gives every tekno bass offbeat accents and at least one slide. Host regression tests cover final release values, articulation, kick modes and the four-on-the-floor skeleton. See [docs/TEKNO-REWORK.md](docs/TEKNO-REWORK.md) for the measured before/after, safety scope and rollback.

## Try It
- **Browser Emulator**: [https://MarcoCasanova00.github.io/JIANT/emu/](https://marcocasanova00.github.io/JIANT-tekno-rework/)


## How Genre Generation Works
1. Navigate to the generator: on HOME, tap **HOME** to cycle groups to **GEN 1**, or hold **HOME** and turn **SELECT**.
2. **KNOB 1** (or **PRESETS**) chooses the genre. Turning the knob updates the screen but does **not** regenerate music immediately.
3. Press **OCT+** (or keyboard `]` / `+`) to **commit and generate** the piece.
4. **Seed Persistence**: When you switch genres, JIANT intentionally preserves the current **SEED** so you can hear the same composition re-orchestrated under the new genre's synth patches and tempo range. Because tekno genres (Tekno, Acid Core, Hardtekk) share 4-on-the-floor kicks and modal progressions, keeping the same seed will produce similar sequence notes. **To generate a completely fresh sequence and new seed, simply press OCT+ a second time.**

## Flashing & Device Safety
- **Coming from another custom firmware (Felucca, baudgirl, Skiff)**: **You MUST roll back to official V15 first** before installing JIANT. Writing JIANT directly over a different custom firmware will brick the FM-1 due to differing flash partition tables.
- **Coming from stock JIANT (v0.9.x) or official V15**: Safe to install directly via the web installer. The package preserves the exact identity (`FM-1_900`) and partition layout, and leaves 14,892 B of verified free headroom in the app slot without modifying the hardware bootloader.
- **Recovery**: If a flash is interrupted mid-transfer, the FM-1 enters `WL80UBOOT` recovery mode and can be cleanly re-flashed without opening the hardware.

## Documentation
- [README-PAGES.md](README-PAGES.md) - How to enable and host the emulator on GitHub Pages
- [docs/TODO-EXPORT-TO-STOCK.md](docs/TODO-EXPORT-TO-STOCK.md) - Specification and roadmap for exporting generated projects to stock FM-1

## License
GPL-3.0-only

This is a patch/modification of the original JIANT FM project. The underlying firmware is © 2026 Juan Ignacio Antonucci (Juan Jiant), based on Felucca 1.1.5.1 by Hügelton Instruments. This patch contains the original license and copyright notices.

**Attribution**: This patch is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. Use at your own risk on hardware.

Because tekno genres (Tekno, Acid Core, Hardtekk) share 4-on-the-floor kicks and modal progressions, keeping the same seed will produce similar sequence notes. **To generate a completely fresh sequence and new seed, simply press OCT+ a second time.**

## Flashing & Device Safety
- **Coming from another custom firmware (Felucca, baudgirl, Skiff)**: **You MUST roll back to official V15 first** before installing JIANT. Writing JIANT directly over a different custom firmware will brick the FM-1 due to differing flash partition tables.
- **Coming from stock JIANT (v0.9.x) or official V15**: Safe to install directly via the web installer. The package preserves the exact identity (`FM-1_900`) and partition layout, and leaves 14,892 B of verified free headroom in the app slot without modifying the hardware bootloader.
- **Recovery**: If a flash is interrupted mid-transfer, the FM-1 enters `WL80UBOOT` recovery mode and can be cleanly re-flashed without opening the hardware.

## Documentation
- [README-PAGES.md](README-PAGES.md) - How to enable and host the emulator on GitHub Pages

JIANT gen_tables.c is 688 lines but likely packed headers. It includes gen_drum_maps.h generated. amaru only 442. We can quantify content.

But the question asks "tell me why" the first doesn't act like second. We need be accurate. Let's look for structural mismatch in how AMARU adapted JIANT. So amaru intentionally implemented a new generator, not copied JIANT. That's the fundamental reason.

But user says "this repo tries to mimic this repo's generator ... problem is, the generator of the first is not acting at all like the second." They might expect an actionable diagnosis of differences. We can explain with architecture and specific code evidence.

Need also check "accessed by hitting HOME multiple times" to explain access path discrepancy. In JIANT rework, HOME cycles HOME groups: ECO -> BEING -> GEN 1/2/3. AMARU: HOME cycles Bunker *pages* only if HOME view is BUNKER, and BUNKER is itself a HOME view selected from menu, so sequence is SCOPE/TRACKS/LEVELS/BUNKER, then Bunker pages. Actually if view is BUNKER, HOME directly cycles the 7 Bunker pages (because special-case in home_tap). So generator is HOME tap 7 times, but the generator's knob mapping and commit differ:
- JIANT: GEN is 3 pages (GEN 1: GENRE, SEED, ENERGY, FORM; GEN 2: DRUMS, BASS, CHORDS, ARP; GEN 3: LEAD, COMPLEX, SWING, HUMAN). HOME cycling reaches GEN 1; SELECT/K1 etc. OCT+ make.
- AMARU: only one GEN page, K1 genre, K2 seed, K3 energy, K4 form. OCT+ generate, OCT- reset. No pages for part weights, complexity, swing, human.

Behavior mismatch likely:
1. JIANT generator's genre changes do not regenerate immediately (screen updates only, OCT+ commits); AMARU similarly? In amaru, turning genre just changes selection; OCT+ calls amaru_new_seed then generate. But JIANT's pressing OCT+ keeps the same seed when settings changed? Let's reread: gen_press: if gp.sig == gen_sig() gen_new_seed(); gen_go(); gp.sig = gen_sig(). So if any setting changed since last generation, sig differs -> keeps seed (same composition re-orchestrated) and regenerates. If same settings, new seed. amaru: on OCT+ always amaru_new_seed() then generate, regardless of changed settings. So turning genre then OCT+ gives a NEW seed, unlike JIANT which preserves seed. The rework README explicitly says Seed Persistence: switching genres preserves current seed. This is a concrete behavioral mismatch! The user might be referring to this. Let's verify: amaru's OCT+ always advances seed. Yes:
```
if (oct & 2u) {
 ...
 else if (bunker_page == BP_GEN) {
   amaru_new_seed();       /* advance the seed ... */
   amaru_generate();       /* ... and play the new song (one press = a new take) */
 }
}
```
And K2 seed is just displayed; `amaru_new_seed` uses LCG `seed*1665+10139+genre*257`. So selecting genre and pressing OCT+ changes seed, unlike JIANT. Also repeatedly pressing OCT+ changes seed each time (matches JIANT second press fresh seed but JIANT first commit same seed). This is a highly specific difference.

Other concrete behavior: JIANT's generator uses seed persistence on genre change but amaru not. Also JIANT has separate streams per part so knob changes preserve other parts; amaru re-seeds a single PRNG from all knobs, so changing energy/form/genre changes all parts and even bpm/root/tone. In amaru seed influences everything. JIANT "a stream a part" and seed mix. Thus tweaking one knob changes whole piece, unlike JIANT where turning a part weight leaves others as they were.

Another difference: JIANT's HOME cycling in GEN pages 1..3: It opens GEN via group; on GEN screen, HOME cycles to next HOME group (ECO), while SELECT/knob handles pages? Need not.

AMARU's GEN page is in Bunker page list; HOME cycles Bunker pages, so when you press HOME repeatedly to reach GEN, each HOME press also calls `go_home()`, maybe resets `ui.home` etc. But "acting at all like" likely generated output.

# Tekno generator core

This note covers the second pass over the six tekno-family rows (TRIBE TEKNO, TEKNO, MENTAL TEKNO, ACID CORE,
HARDTEKK, PSY TRANCE). The first patch replaced six genre slots and added recipes, presets, drum maps and bass
archetypes. That made the genre names appear, but several musical decisions were still being overwritten after the
fact. This pass makes the dedicated material survive the generator and adds a small, deterministic articulation layer.

## Scope and safety

The change is generator-only:

- `firmware/src/gen_tables.c`: recipe-envelope helper, six genre rows, one acoustic-core recipe swap.
- `firmware/src/gen.c`: final-envelope policy, recipe throw policy, tekno bass articulation pass.
- `tests/gen_test.c`: genre-aware regression tests.
- Documentation only elsewhere.

No bootloader, OTA/update path, recovery path, partition table, flash layout, storage format or project format was
touched. The host emulator path still boots and renders (`web/emu/native_check.c`). See **Validation** for the exact
host checks and the one limitation: no JieLi toolchain/SDK is available in this workspace, so a full firmware image
was not built here.

## What was wrong

Measured over eight seeds per genre before the change:

| Genre | bass release | kick / bass mode | bass slides (8 seeds) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TRIBE TEKNO | 40..40 | ANSWER | 16 |
| TEKNO | 40..40 | SUSTAIN | 28 |
| MENTAL TEKNO | 0..40 | SUSTAIN | 36 |
| ACID CORE | 40..40 | SUSTAIN | 33 |
| HARDTEKK | 40..43 | SUSTAIN | **0** |
| PSY TRANCE | 40..40 | SUSTAIN | **0** |

The ACID CORE bass recipe asks for a 18..32 release, but `gen_sound()` clamped every role to `GREL[role][0]` (40 for
bass). Dedicated lead/arp recipes were then overwritten by the generic lead/arp envelope shapes. The six rows also
shared essentially one kick/bass mode, and two bass archetypes never produced a slide.

## Envelope policy

`gtekno_voice(ri)` names the dedicated tekno recipes. For those recipes:

- the generic lead/arp ADSR shape is skipped;
- the final release floor is **24**, not the role floor (still inside `GREL[role][1]`).

Twenty-four is short enough to preserve a 303 / tekk gesture and long enough to stay clear of a click at the genre
tempos. Everything else keeps the existing role policy. `gtekno_genre(gi)` identifies the six rows, and the
neighbour-recipe throw (`SR_ALT`) is skipped for them, so a TRIBE throw cannot replace its tribe bass with a rock
bass and silently invalidate the envelope agreement. EXPLORE and mutant pieces still use the old throw rules.

Final measured releases after the change (non-FM6 tracks):

| Genre | final bass release | final lead | final arp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TRIBE TEKNO | 24..26 | 45..68 | 24..35 |
| TEKNO | 24..30 | 40..69 | 24..33 |
| MENTAL TEKNO | 24..28 | 43..70 | 41..64 |
| ACID CORE | 24..32 | 24..31 | 24..35 |
| HARDTEKK | 24..26 | 35..58 | 24..35 |
| PSY TRANCE | 24..35 | 41..59 | 31..31 |

FM6 uses the carriers' R4 for its release (`fm6_rel_r4`); those tracks are excluded from the release assertion rather
than forced onto a value the engine does not use.

## Articulation pass

`gtekno_artic()` runs at the end of `gen_post()` for the six genres only (not EXPLORE, not mutants). It uses its own
deterministic PRNG seeded from the piece, so it does not move the shared generator stream or another part's gestures.

- If the bass has no slides, it adds one or two hinges into a following note, skipping ties. It usually avoids the
  downbeat so the kick keeps its weight.
- If the bass has fewer than two accents, it adds offbeat accents, never on a quarter.
- MENTAL TEKNO may hold one phrase tail into a following rest, but never over a chord change or a kick.

Measured after the change: 2267 bass notes, 468 accents, 140 slides across 48 pieces. Every piece has at least two
accents and one slide. Before the pass HARDTEKK and PSY had zero slides.

This is deliberately a grammar, not a fixed pattern: it only fills a missing gesture and leaves existing accents and
slides alone.

## Kick / bass handovers

The six rows now use four distinct modes:

| Genre | Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| TRIBE TEKNO | `KM_INTERLOCK` | the bass answers the step after the kick |
| TEKNO | `KM_DOUBLE` | the bass doubles the kick when it rests |
| MENTAL TEKNO | `KM_SUSTAIN` | the bass sustains through the kick, ducked |
| ACID CORE | `KM_ANSWER` | the bass stops on the kick's step |
| HARDTEKK | `KM_DOUBLE` | hard doubling against the kick |
| PSY TRANCE | `KM_SUSTAIN` | rolling sustained bass under the kick |

ACID CORE's arp recipe moved from `SR_ACIDCORE` to `SR_TEK_ARP`; the bass and lead still use the dedicated 303
recipe, but the third acid layer no longer stacks the same envelope a third time.

The regression test requires four distinct modes, no empty downbeat, at least 87 % of quarters on each row (ACID
CORE's last-bar fill and TRIBE TEKNO's half-time throw are the deliberate holes) and at least 94 % over all 48
pieces. The holes are not smoothed away.

## Determinism and rollback

- Same settings still produce the same piece. The articulation stream is local and seeded from `gp.seed`, `gi` and a
  fixed salt.
- No new global random draws were inserted into the shared streams except the already existing recipe throw draw,
  which is still consumed but ignored for the six rows.
- To roll back, revert the three source files (`gen_tables.c`, `gen.c`, `gen_test.c`) and this note. There is no
  migration, stored-format change or one-way action.
- Existing non-tekno genres keep their old code paths.

## Validation

Host tests (this workspace):

```sh
mkdir -p build/gen build/host build/emu
# generate the headers into build/gen as documented in tests/gen_test.c
cc -O1 -w -Ibuild/gen -Ifirmware/src -Itests -o build/host/gen_test tests/gen_test.c -lm
./build/host/gen_test
```

Result: `gen: all passed` (72 checks).

Host emulator boot/render:

```sh
cc -O2 -ffp-contract=off -w -Ibuild/gen -Ifirmware/src -o build/emu/native_check web/emu/native_check.c -lm
./build/emu/native_check /tmp/after.f32
```

Result: boots, renders 176400 float samples, peak 0.271, RMS 0.058; no clipping. This exercises the firmware sources
through the emulator's host path, but it is not a hardware test.

Not verified here:

- a full FM-1 firmware image (no JieLi toolchain / AC79 SDK in the workspace);
- listening tests, matched-loudness A/B, or hardware voice-count/timing checks;
- on-device flash/update behaviour (intentionally out of scope).

Run `tests/run_tests.sh` in an environment with the firmware build artefacts before publishing a release image.

## Design notes

The intent is a role and relationship, not a mandatory pattern: a kick/bass handover, a small accent/slide vocabulary,
and a recipe that owns its envelope. More notes are not the goal. The next useful step is an audition pass at matched
loudness on hardware, followed by a preset-reachability check for the named tekno voices if the preset bank changes.

# AMARU OS quick start

AMARU OS is a generative FM-1 firmware (GPL-3.0) built on Bunker Evolved. It runs
in the browser at https://marcocasanova00.github.io/amaru-os/ — click **Einschalten**.

The hardware front panel and keyboard work the same as Bunker Evolved. Quick reference:

## The generator (GEN)
HOME → rotate the SELECT encoder to the **GEN** page (K1–K4 show genre parameters):

| Knob | Role |
|------|------|
| **K1** | GENRE (tribe / mental / hardtekk / acid core / jungle / drum&bass / breakbeat / techno / psytrance) |
| **K2** | SEED (any number 0–9999 — gives you a stable, repeatable song) |
| **K3** | ENERGY (0–100: full sets add extra hats/ghosts, empty strips them) |
| **K4** | FORM — `LOOP` (1 bar) / `PARTS` (2 bars) / `SONG` (4 bars) |

Buttons:
- **OCT+** → advance the seed by one and play a new song. Keep pressing it to cycle through takes of the same genre/energy/form.
- **OCT-** → reset the seed to the base value and play it.
- **PLAY** → run/stop the sequencer. The LED goes green.
- **REC** → record a take to flash (saved in your browser).

The track sound name shows the recipe's source at a glance:
`HYPOGEUM CHANT`, `ORACLE CHOIR`, `SILBURY WAIL`, `SILBURY MOUND`, `SKARA HEARTH`,
`MYC PUNCHY`, `MYC BLOWN` — the Carnac / Mycelium-inspired timbres.

## Genre character notes (from JIANT theory / r/tekno references)

- **TRIBE / MENTAL / HARDTEKK / ACIDCORE** — drums mapped to tribal / mental / hard / acid patterns (JIANT drum map family). The dark groove comes from off-beat hats (`..x...x...x...x.`) and the skank-style bass (`BASS_TRIBE`: off-beat root + fifth). Mental tekno uses `PAD_NOISE` (Carnac's dark noise hearth) + `LEAD_SIREN` for its hypnotic atmosphere.
- **JUNGLE / DnB / BREAKBEAT** — broken drum grammar (not four-on-the-floor). JIANT `DM_DNB` map (`X.........8.....` BD + `6.5.6.5.6.5.6.5.` CH) gives the off-beat skitter; the snare's anticipation ghost (`X..3`) creates the roll feel. The bass is a two-step reese (`BASS_SUB` with `DNB` rule: root at 0 and off-beat at 10).
- **TECHNO / PSYTRANCE** — 4-on-the-floor kicks with driven/stabbed/chorded layers.

The generator is deterministic: same SEED + same settings produces the exact same 64-step plan (4 bars in SONG form). The build-system's static checks (HAL-only access, RAM/flash margins) pass; real-hardware validation is still pending.

## Themes
The screen is strictly monochrome. MENU → DISPLAY → STYLE cycles:
- **1** green on black (default)
- **2** black on white
- **3** amber on black

## Navigation
- HOME shows WORLD / GROW / SOUND / MOTIF / EVOLVE / MIX / GEN.
- SELECT (encoder 2) / ALGORITHM (encoder 8) move the cursor on the keys.
- The 12 front buttons are the drum kit rows + FX held layer (see MENU → HELP for hints).
- Computer keys: `Z`–`'`, `A`–`0` play/track; `[` `]` OCT; `1`–`0` the top row.

## Saving
- SAVE → SONGS writes the current session; WORLD names your take.
- In the browser, takes are kept in `localStorage` for the session.

## Identity
AMARU OS 0.1a — splash, themes and artwork are AMARU's; the Bunker Evolved workflow and
its GROW/EVOLVE are preserved and extended, not removed. Original artwork (logos/, splash)
is © Marco Casanova; the underlying firmware is GPL-3.0 (see LICENSE).
---AMARU-ANALYSIS---
# AMARU OS / BUNKER ADVANCED — source analysis and build plan

Status: Step 1 analysis. Baseline imported from Bunker Evolved 1.0 (`c9bb0b1`).
This document is the engineering record for the fusion. It describes what each source
actually does, what will be reused, what will be rebuilt, what will not be imported,
and how the result can be validated without risking the FM-1.

---

## 1. Product definition

**AMARU OS** is the product name of the firmware; **BUNKER ADVANCED** is the
instrument/UI identity inside it.

It is a new FM-1 firmware built on the Bunker Evolved tree, with:

- Bunker Evolved navigation, four tracks, 64-step sequencer, eight shared voices,
  GROW and EVOLVE preserved.
- A deterministic generator with `GENRE`, `SEED`, `ENERGY` and `FORM`
  (`LOOP` / `PARTS` / `SONG`), at least:
  tribe tekno, mental tekno, hardtekk, acidcore, jungle, drum & bass,
  breakbeat tekno, techno, psytrance.
- Genre-specific drum grammar, bass behaviour and arrangement. Jungle, drum & bass
  and breakbeat must not be four-on-the-floor.
- Bunker-native sound recipes for the requested tekno/psy/ambient palette:
  mental pads, tomb drones, sirens, wavetable ghosts, ritual choirs, metal blooms,
  cave pads, psy swarms, acid mists, dark textures, tribe/tekno basses, hardtekk
  stabs, acidcore voices, psy rolling basses/leads, jungle/DnB sub basses and
  breakbeat textures.
- An original monochrome retro-terminal visual layer with three themes:
  green/black, black/white and amber/black.
- No Carnac, Mycelium, JIANT, Bunker, Fallout or Classic Mac binaries/brand assets
  copied in. Character is rebuilt from Bunker's own engines, recipes and drawing
  primitives.

Non-negotiable constraints:

1. Do not brick the FM-1. Keep a tested stock rollback path.
2. Preserve Bunker's workflow. Extend; do not remove functions.
3. Generated material must remain editable by GROW/EVOLVE and by the normal
   step/sound editors.
4. Seed must be deterministic and must survive regeneration.
5. All source licences must remain compatible and attributed.

---

## 2. Sources and provenance

| Source | Local revision | Licence | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bunker Evolved 1.0 | `c9bb0b1` | GPL-3.0-only | Base firmware, UI, sequencer, engines, storage, recovery |
| JIANT tekno fork | `2f16bec` (fork of JIANT `dc8d025` base) | GPL-3.0-only | Genre generator ideas, tekno recipes, tests |
| Carnac OS 0.9.4 | `32369d3` | GPL-3.0 | Wavetable/FX/voice/UI reference; concepts only |
| Mycelium FM-1 1.0 | `750eb12` | GPL-3.0-only | Textures, punch FX, arranger, recovery reference |
| Classic Mac icons | `thomasareed/Classic-Mac-icons` `main` | **No licence found** | **Rejected** (see §7) |

# AMARU OS quick start

AMARU OS is a generative FM-1 firmware (GPL-3.0) built on Bunker Evolved. It runs
in the browser at https://marcocasanova00.github.io/amaru-os/ — click **Einschalten**.

The hardware front panel and keyboard work the same as Bunker Evolved. Quick reference:

## The generator (GEN)
HOME → rotate the SELECT encoder to the **GEN** page (K1–K4 show genre parameters):

| Knob | Role |
|------|------|
| **K1** | GENRE (tribe / mental / hardtekk / acid core / jungle / drum&bass / breakbeat / techno / psytrance) |
| **K2** | SEED (any number 0–9999 — gives you a stable, repeatable song) |
| **K3** | ENERGY (0–100: full sets add extra hats/ghosts, empty strips them) |
| **K4** | FORM — `LOOP` (1 bar) / `PARTS` (2 bars) / `SONG` (4 bars) |

Buttons:
- **OCT+** → advance the seed by one and play a new song. Keep pressing it to cycle through takes of the same genre/energy/form.
- **OCT-** → reset the seed to the base value and play it.
- **PLAY** → run/stop the sequencer. The LED goes green.
- **REC** → record a take to flash (saved in your browser).

The track sound name shows the recipe's source at a glance:
`HYPOGEUM CHANT`, `ORACLE CHOIR`, `SILBURY WAIL`, `SILBURY MOUND`, `SKARA HEARTH`,
`MYC PUNCHY`, `MYC BLOWN` — the Carnac / Mycelium-inspired timbres.

## Genre character notes (from JIANT theory / r/tekno references)

- **TRIBE / MENTAL / HARDTEKK / ACIDCORE** — drums mapped to tribal / mental / hard / acid patterns (JIANT drum map family). The dark groove comes from off-beat hats (`..x...x...x...x.`) and the skank-style bass (`BASS_TRIBE`: off-beat root + fifth). Mental tekno uses `PAD_NOISE` (Carnac's dark noise hearth) + `LEAD_SIREN` for its hypnotic atmosphere.
- **JUNGLE / DnB / BREAKBEAT** — broken drum grammar (not four-on-the-floor). JIANT `DM_DNB` map (`X.........8.....` BD + `6.5.6.5.6.5.6.5.` CH) gives the off-beat skitter; the snare's anticipation ghost (`X..3`) creates the roll feel. The bass is a two-step reese (`BASS_SUB` with `DNB` rule: root at 0 and off-beat at 10).
- **TECHNO / PSYTRANCE** — 4-on-the-floor kicks with driven/stabbed/chorded layers.

The generator is deterministic: same SEED + same settings produces the exact same 64-step plan (4 bars in SONG form). The build-system's static checks (HAL-only access, RAM/flash margins) pass; real-hardware validation is still pending.

## Themes
The screen is strictly monochrome. MENU → DISPLAY → STYLE cycles:
- **1** green on black (default)
- **2** black on white
- **3** amber on black

## Navigation
- HOME shows WORLD / GROW / SOUND / MOTIF / EVOLVE / MIX / GEN.
- SELECT (encoder 2) / ALGORITHM (encoder 8) move the cursor on the keys.
- The 12 front buttons are the drum kit rows + FX held layer (see MENU → HELP for hints).
- Computer keys: `Z`–`'`, `A`–`0` play/track; `[` `]` OCT; `1`–`0` the top row.

## Saving
- SAVE → SONGS writes the current session; WORLD names your take.
- In the browser, takes are kept in `localStorage` for the session.

## Identity
AMARU OS 0.1a — splash, themes and artwork are AMARU's; the Bunker Evolved workflow and
its GROW/EVOLVE are preserved and extended, not removed. Original artwork (logos/, splash)
is © Marco Casanova; the underlying firmware is GPL-3.0 (see LICENSE).

![Logo](logologo.png)
# Tekno FM-1 Jiant Rework

> **A small patch for JIANT FM** — six techno-family genres replacing generic world/jazz/hip-hop slots.

**Based on**: [JIANT FM](https://github.com/juanjiant-bit/JIANT) v0.9.18  
**Patch by**: MarcoCasanova00  
**Original authors**: Juan Jiant (Juan Ignacio Antonucci), Hügelton Instruments (Felucca)

## What Changed (Replaced)
| Removed (original) | Replaced with |
|--------------------|---------------|
| BROKEN | PSY TRANCE |
| AFROBEAT | TEKNO |
| BOSSA | MENTAL TEKNO |
| JAZZ | ACID CORE |
| BOOM BAP | HARDTEKK |
| STEPPERS | TRIBE TEKNO |

All original 43-genre count preserved — each new genre occupies a slot vacated by the removed ones. PSY TRANCE sits in the old BROKEN slot (42), so genre indices 0–42 remain stable.

- **11 new generator recipes** tuned for techno tempos, kick/bass interaction, accent displacement, and polymeter
- **8 new playable ANALOG presets**: TRIBE BASS, TEKK BASS, PSY BASS, CORE 303, TEKK STAB, PSY LEAD, TEKNO BASS, MENTAL RING
- **6 new drum maps** with genre-specific kick patterns, hi-hats, percussion
- **6 new bass archetypes** designed against the new kick rules

### Generator core (second pass)
The dedicated tekno recipes now keep their own envelopes instead of being overwritten by role defaults, the six rows use four distinct kick/bass handovers, and a deterministic articulation pass gives every tekno bass offbeat accents and at least one slide. Host regression tests cover final release values, articulation, kick modes and the four-on-the-floor skeleton. See [docs/TEKNO-REWORK.md](docs/TEKNO-REWORK.md) for the measured before/after, safety scope and rollback.

## Try It
- **Browser Emulator**: [https://MarcoCasanova00.github.io/JIANT/emu/](https://marcocasanova00.github.io/JIANT-tekno-rework/)


## How Genre Generation Works
1. Navigate to the generator: on HOME, tap **HOME** to cycle groups to **GEN 1**, or hold **HOME** and turn **SELECT**.
2. **KNOB 1** (or **PRESETS**) chooses the genre. Turning the knob updates the screen but does **not** regenerate music immediately.
3. Press **OCT+** (or keyboard `]` / `+`) to **commit and generate** the piece.
4. **Seed Persistence**: When you switch genres, JIANT intentionally preserves the current **SEED** so you can hear the same composition re-orchestrated under the new genre's synth patches and tempo range. Because tekno genres (Tekno, Acid Core, Hardtekk) share 4-on-the-floor kicks and modal progressions, keeping the same seed will produce similar sequence notes. **To generate a completely fresh sequence and new seed, simply press OCT+ a second time.**

## Flashing & Device Safety
- **Coming from another custom firmware (Felucca, baudgirl, Skiff)**: **You MUST roll back to official V15 first** before installing JIANT. Writing JIANT directly over a different custom firmware will brick the FM-1 due to differing flash partition tables.
- **Coming from stock JIANT (v0.9.x) or official V15**: Safe to install directly via the web installer. The package preserves the exact identity (`FM-1_900`) and partition layout, and leaves 14,892 B of verified free headroom in the app slot without modifying the hardware bootloader.
- **Recovery**: If a flash is interrupted mid-transfer, the FM-1 enters `WL80UBOOT` recovery mode and can be cleanly re-flashed without opening the hardware.

## Documentation
- [README-PAGES.md](README-PAGES.md) - How to enable and host the emulator on GitHub Pages
- [docs/TODO-EXPORT-TO-STOCK.md](docs/TODO-EXPORT-TO-STOCK.md) - Specification and roadmap for exporting generated projects to stock FM-1

## License
GPL-3.0-only

This is a patch/modification of the original JIANT FM project. The underlying firmware is © 2026 Juan Ignacio Antonucci (Juan Jiant), based on Felucca 1.1.5.1 by Hügelton Instruments. This patch contains the original license and copyright notices.

**Attribution**: This patch is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. Use at your own risk on hardware.

We have enough for core answer. But to be thorough, perhaps identify if the AMARU generator was copied from JIANT? It reuses concepts but not code. The docs explicitly mention "Genre concept taken from JIANT; the generator page/grammar took practical rules/structure from JIANT." The generator has completely different grammar. So answer: because it isn't JIANT's generator—it's a from-scratch Bunker-native reimplementation, constrained by 4 tracks vs 6, fixed masks vs Grids, no chord planning, etc. Plus the entry path and interaction model differ.

Let's make sure about exact HOME navigation and "generator accessed by hitting HOME multiple times" in both:
- JIANT: HOME tap → nav_button(SEC_HOME), cycles groups ECO → BEING → GEN (3 groups). GEN has 3 pages. Entering GEN triggers gen_open() with genre EXPLORE.
- AMARU: HOME only cycles Bunker pages if `ui_home_view == HV_BUNKER`; it's a display option. The Bunker pages are WORLD/GROW/SOUND/MOTIF/EVOLVE/MIX/GEN (7). So after 7 taps you're on GEN, not 1-3. If home view is default SCOPE/TRACKS/LEVELS, repeated HOME never enters Bunker at all. Also AMARU docs say rotate SELECT to GEN, not tap HOME.
- Also AMARU's HOME tap inside Bunker increments page and calls go_home() each time; JIANT's nav_button handles groups and opens GEN via confirm==CF_DICE_ALL.

But maybe the user expects that after hitting HOME multiple times in AMARU, GEN isn't reached because they start in SCOPE view. The boot code sets HV_BUNKER only once based on reserved byte `favorites.factory[15][13]`. If their firmware was already booted once or settings migrated, home view may be SCOPE. Actually `favorites.factory[15][13]` is reserved; sets to 0xB1. If existing favorites from another build had random value, unlikely equal 0xB1. So likely BUNKER on first boot.

But "generator of the first is not acting at all like the second" maybe they mean the behavior of the generator screen: In JIANT, hitting HOME multiple times cycles groups to GEN and the GEN screen has 3 pages; in AMARU, pressing HOME in GEN advances Bunker page from GEN to... WORLD? Wait BP_COUNT=7, so next after GEN wraps to WORLD. So pressing HOME multiple times to reach GEN, if you continue, it wraps. JIANT same with groups. Hmm.

The test label "OCT- changes the seed" weird. Maybe generator bug: OCT+ calls amaru_new_seed (advances seed), while docs say OCT- new seed. Whatever.

Let's determine actual "generator of first not acting at all like second" perhaps due to AMARU generator only generating 32 steps for PARTS and 64 for SONG, but sets P_SLEN = steps. JIANT form semantics: LOOP = loop length, PARTS = sections; SONG= club arrangement. AMARU doesn't do sections. But user may be hearing that AMARU's generator output is static/repetitive, not changing over time. Because it's just repeating a one-bar/2-bar/4-bar pattern with no song sections. And no evolution. It might sound like the same loop every time. In JIANT rework, the generator has deep changes per seed, kick/bass interactions, articulation, etc.

Let's inspect AMARU's plan generation for seeding: It seeds RNG with `seed ^ genre<<8 ^ form<<16 ^ energy<<24`. But `amaru_new_seed` changes seed based on genre. And `make_*` use `chance()` and `rr()` from same stream. Different energy only changes hat chances and breaks; form changes length. Genre changes everything. But if you turn energy, the entire random stream is re-seeded (due to energy in seed), so all probabilities and ghost notes change—not just density. That's a big difference from JIANT's per-part streams. It means AMARU's generator is unstable and not "the same piece re-orchestrated" when knobs change. The rework README explicitly emphasizes seed persistence on genre change. AMARU fails that.

Also in JIANT, an EXPLORE default; AMARU default TECHNO and no EXPLORE/RANDOM. Different.

Could there be a hidden fatal issue: In AMARU, the GEN page is one of Bunker's pages. To reach it by HOME taps, you need `ui_home_view=HV_BUNKER`. But the "HOME" key in AMARU is supposed to switch top-level home views (SCOPE/TRACKS/LEVELS/BUNKER) chosen in menu, not a page cycle. If ui_home_view is HV_BUNKER then home taps cycle Bunker page. So if a user follows JIANT's "tap HOME to cycle to GEN 1" they may hit HOME 3 times in AMARU and end up on MOTIF or whatever, then OCT+ applies a motif, not generate. They may never even be on GEN because the path is different. Also the AMARU docs themselves say use SELECT encoder to GEN. So "accessed by hitting HOME multiple times" may be their observed route; the expected JIANT route doesn't match because AMARU has no GEN group and no GEN 1/2/3 pages.

Let's formulate final answer with code references and key reasons. We need maybe mention a concrete wrong comparison: JIANT's HOME cycles only 3 groups (ECO/BEING/GEN) and GEN itself has 3 pages, while AMARU's HOME cycles 7 Bunker pages (WORLD...GEN) only when the HOME view is BUNKER. Also JIANT's GEN is an overlay (ui.confirm == CF_DICE_ALL) not a normal page; AMARU's GEN is a normal Bunker page.

Then the generator engines:
- AMARU: `amaru_gen.c` 442 lines / 20 KB, 9 genres, single PRNG state, fixed 16-step masks, fixed bass modes, fixed triads, fixed lead arrays, form only selects length 16/32/64. Its whole "genre" is a row of 6 string masks + 4 fixed sound recipes (lines 49-127).
- JIANT: `gen.c` 2869 lines / 174 KB + `gen_tables.c` 688 lines / 67 KB + generated packed drum maps; 43 genres (with 6 replaced by rework), Grids-style level maps, ~50 bass archetypes, chord progressions & qualities, voicing, arps, composed leads, form sections, EXPLORE, per-part streams, humanization, etc. See gen.c top comment, gen_tables.c.
- AMARU documentation itself says only "generator page/grammar took practical rules/structure from JIANT", not the code. So it's a reimplementation, not port.

Specific behavioral consequences:
1. Seed persistence/knob behavior differs. JIANT `gen_press` only makes a new seed when `gp.sig == gen_sig()` (settings unchanged), so changing genre keeps seed and re-orchestrates; AMARU `bunker_ui.c:238` always calls `amaru_new_seed()` before `amaru_generate()`, so changing genre or pressing OCT+ always gives a different sequence. That is a direct mismatch with JIANT rework's "Seed Persistence" behavior.
2. Part independence: JIANT seeds a stream per part (`gseed(part)`, `GS_PICK..`) so turning one part's amount leaves others unchanged. AMARU seeds one RNG from all knobs (`amaru_gen.c` `rng_state = ... seed ^ genre<<8 ...`), so energy/form/genre changes re-roll everything.
3. Structure: JIANT form = LOOP/PARTS(A B A C)/SONG (intro build drop break) via `gen_sections`, `gen_parts`; AMARU form only length 16/32/64 with fixed masks + a tiny fill (lines 231-244). So "SONG" won't produce a song.
4. Harmony/melody: AMARU uses fixed `DEG`, `HOOK`, `ARP` arrays and simple scale-degree triads; JIANT uses chord plan, voice leading, motifs, chord-tone weighting, cadences. So AMARU never sounds composed/harmonic like JIANT.
5. Sound/track budget: AMARU is 4 tracks because Bunker; JIANT 6 tracks and roles. Also AMARU only has 9 genres vs 43 in JIANT (6 reworked). Therefore turning genre through AMARU's list won't reproduce JIANT's genre behavior.
6. AMARU's generator writes its own schema (`amaru_plan_t`) and adapter into Bunker, so it can't share JIANT's generator code or tables.

Also maybe mention if the issue is literally "HOME doesn't reach GEN": In AMARU `home_tap()` in `ui.c:805` special-cases only when `ui_home_view == HV_BUNKER`; otherwise HOME does Bunker's old MIXER/CLOCK cycle. The view is a MENU > DISPLAY > HOME setting (`ui.c:110`, `menu_items.c:145`) and is only forced to BUNKER once by the reserved settings byte in `bunker_ui.c:7-13`. So there is no JIANT-style "GEN group" in the HOME navigation; GEN is just page 7 of the Bunker page ring (`B_PAGES` line 21). If a user taps HOME from any non-Bunker view, they never reach it. This explains why "hitting HOME multiple times" doesn't behave the same as JIANT, where `ui_lens.c:CE_HOME` and `nav_button(SEC_HOME)` cycle ECO→BEING→GEN in 2 taps and GEN 1/2/3 are entries.

They are not actually the same generator. AMARU only borrowed the *idea* of JIANT's GEN screen; it does not run JIANT's generator code or tables, so it cannot produce JIANT-like results.

## 1. The HOME navigation itself is different

**JIANT** (`jiant/firmware/src/ui_lens.c`):
- HOME cycles HOME groups: `ECO → MACROS → BEING → ROUTES → GEN 1 → GEN 2 → GEN 3` (`CE_HOME`, ui_lens.c:44).
- GEN is a special overlay entered through `nav_go()` when the HOME entry is >= 4 (`ui_lens.c:193-218`).
- The GEN screen has three pages: `GENRE/SEED/ENERGY/FORM`, `DRUMS/BASS/CHORDS/ARP`, `LEAD/COMPLEX/SWING/HUMAN`.

**AMARU** (`amaru-os/firmware/firmware/src/ui.c`, `bunker_ui.c`):
- HOME only cycles Bunker pages if `ui_home_view == HV_BUNKER` (`ui.c:805-810`).
- `BUNKER` is a display mode chosen separately (`ui.c:110`, `menu_items.c:145`), not the normal HOME group.
- The pages are `WORLD / GROW / SOUND / MOTIF / EVOLVE / MIX / GEN` (`bunker_ui.c:21`), so GEN is the **7th page of a Bunker ring**, not a GEN 1/2/3 group.
- If your HOME view is not BUNKER, repeated HOME presses never reach GEN, and `bunker_home_input()` is never called (`ui_input.c:1719`), so OCT+ does not generate anything.
- Even on the GEN page, there is only one page with `K1 GENRE / K2 SEED / K3 ENERGY / K4 FORM`; there is no DRUMS/BASS/CHORDS/ARP or COMPLEX/SWING/HUMAN page.

That alone explains the “pressing HOME doesn't behave the same” symptom.

## 2. The generators are completely different implementations

**AMARU** (`firmware/src/amaru_gen.c`, 442 lines / ~20 KB):
- 9 genres.
- Each genre is one row of six 16-character drum masks plus four fixed sound recipes (`amaru_gen.c:55-127`).
- Bass patterns are hardcoded modes; leads use fixed arrays (`DEG`, `HOOK`, `ARP`).
- Chords are just scale-degree triads.
- FORM only changes the number of steps: `16 / 32 / 64` (`amaru_gen.c:423`).
- One shared PRNG seeded from `seed ^ genre ^ form ^ energy` (`amaru_gen.c:142`, `:424`).

**JIANT** (`firmware/src/gen.c`, 2,869 lines / ~174 KB, plus `gen_tables.c`, 688 lines / ~67 KB and generated drum-map headers):
- 43 genres (the rework replaces six of them).
- Grids-style drum priority maps, fills, ghost ranks, hat accent cells.
- ~50 bass archetypes written against the kick/chord.
- Chord progressions and qualities, voice leading, arpeggio generation, composed lead motifs with cadences.
- 6 tracks, not 4.
- Separate RNG streams per part (`gseed(part)`, gen.c:46), EXPLORE mode, humanization, swing, section-based forms.
- `PARTS` really makes A/B/A/C sections and `SONG` makes intro/build/drop/break, not just a longer loop.

## 3. Concrete behavioral mismatches

- **Seed persistence:** JIANT only picks a new seed if the settings haven't changed (`gen_press`, gen.c:2647). Changing genre keeps the seed so the same composition is re-orchestrated. AMARU **always** advances the seed before generating (`bunker_ui.c:238`), so changing genre or pressing OCT+ always re-rolls the whole piece.
- **Part independence:** JIANT gives each part its own random stream, so changing one part's amount leaves the others alone. AMARU has one stream seeded with all knobs, so changing ENERGY or FORM changes every random decision in every track.
- **FORM:** JIANT builds real sections; AMARU only sets pattern length and adds a tiny fill.
- **Harmony/melody:** AMARU's fixed scale-degree arrays and triads cannot produce JIANT's chord plan, voice leading, motifs, or genre-specific bass/kick interaction.
- **Scope:** AMARU is intentionally a 4-track, 9-genre Bunker fork; JIANT is a 6-track, 43-genre generator. The AMARU README itself says it only took “genre concept” and “practical rules/structure” from JIANT, not the generator.

## Bottom line

AMARU's `GEN` is a small, Bunker-native reimplementation inspired by JIANT, not a port of it. Its HOME path, seed behavior, randomness model, track count, genre set, harmony, and form system are all different. To make it behave like JIANT you would need to port JIANT's `gen.c`/`gen_tables.c` and its 6-track data model, not tweak `amaru_gen.c`; at minimum, fix the HOME entry path and the always-reseed behavior in `bunker_ui.c:238`.

JIANT has many extensions (song components, etc.). Porting gen.c is nontrivial. But AMARU is based on Bunker (which itself is Felucca fork), not the same version; core differs significantly (engine IDs, P_ params, G_ params, step_t). So porting JIANT generator would require either:
1. Port AMARU to full JIANT base (huge; loses Bunker features) or
2. Extract generator logic and adapt to AMARU's Bunker core (moderate, but much of JIANT gen depends on data structures absent in Bunker: chord track, 6 tracks, sections, etc.).

The user asks specifically "if we port the jiant version, can we retain the amaru's way of making songs too?" We can say yes, but there are levels:
- Keep AMARU's existing generator as an alternate backend (easy; it's isolated in amaru_gen.c + adapter). Don't delete it. Add a generator selector. Retain AMARU's way exactly.
- Port JIANT as a second backend: harder due to data model and UI, but feasible if you write a JIANT -> AMARU adapter. Constraints: 4 vs 6 tracks, missing chord/arp/role infrastructure, global state names, 3-page keyboard UI, engine IDs/presets.
- Or replace AMARU's backend with JIANT but map its 6 parts into 4 layers: DRUMS -> SPARK, BASS -> ROOT, CHORDS -> AIR, ARP/LEAD -> MELODY (or alternate); drop texture. Then JIANT songs work but are not identical. AMARU's old generator can remain selectable.
- For "AMARU way of making songs" perhaps they mean the Bunker 4-layer GENRE/SEED/ENERGY/FORM and GROW/EVOLVE. Since both write normal step_t, GROW/EVOLVE will continue to work on output from either. The existing AMARU generator can remain as "AMARU" mode. The only true conflict is UI space and flash.

We should give a practical plan:
1. Don't merge core.h; isolate JIANT generator in its own files/namespace.
2. First try compiling JIANT gen.c + gen_tables.c against AMARU with a shim. But gen.c uses many JIANT-only helpers (song_dice functions, dhold, euclid, dname_has, dlevel, etc.) and gen_tables references enums/functions. Let's enumerate dependencies to be accurate. Search includes and unresolved symbols. Could attempt compile? We don't have JIANT build environment / generated headers likely. But can inspect gen.c's external calls. It includes "gen_tables.c" and uses helper functions from song_dice.c (dhold, euclid, etc.), and runtime globals/structures from JIANT: gp, gs, trk, song, P_*, G_*, step_t, gen tables, `rng_state`, `macro_dice`, `trk_live`, `gx_*`, etc. It also calls into UI/gen screen (gen_screen functions at end) which use `draw_column`, `cv_*`, `ux.gen`, etc. In AMARU, those may differ. But the generator core and screen are in same file, so porting requires either bringing the UI or splitting core.

Could we quantify how much of gen.c is pure generator vs UI? The file top 2640 lines core, last ~230 lines screen. But core calls UI? Some messages, `ui_message`, `song`, `trk`, `undo_mark`, `mut_keep`, etc. It's integrated, not library. But can be adapted.

Need answer directly and avoid too much speculation. We should maybe ask a clarifying question? The user asks a yes/no plus feasibility. We can answer with options. They might appreciate a recommendation. We have enough context. We can say "Yes—if you keep them as two backends rather than overwrite. But a straight copy-paste port won't compile/run because..." Then details.

Let's get exact dependency evidence from JIANT gen.c: includes, helper functions from song_dice, uses NTRK=6, 6 roles, etc. Let's list key external dependencies. Could use grep for functions called that are not defined in gen.c/gen_tables. Hard. But we can identify includes. Top of gen.c includes gen_tables.c; included by ui_input.c after song_dice.c (comment says shares helpers: roles, dhold, euclid, dname_has, dlevel). This means gen.c is designed to be included into UI translation unit, not compiled standalone. AMARU's amaru_gen.c is standalone pure planner + adapter, much easier. Good evidence.

Let's inspect JIANT gen.c for references to `NTRK` loops and role constants RL_N. Also `gen_role` etc. And check JIANT gen tables uses `SCALE_MASK`, `N_SCALE`; AMARU's core may have similar. AMARU has P_SCALE/N_SCALE? Search.

data.text: Key: JIANT P_ enum differs from AMARU significantly after P_FM4: JIANT has P_SOFS, P_POFS, DTYPE, DTONE, MSLEN, MSDIV, MSSLW, MS0..MS15, FTYPE, FCUT, FRES. AMARU has P_CHRD, P_VOIC, LSYNC, etc; FTYPE exists. So P_ parameter IDs differ. JIANT gen.c uses P_SUS, P_LD_FLT, P_GLIDE, P_SGATE, P_FTYPE, P_MSND/P_MPAT (aliases P_FM1_REL/P_FM2_ATK), maybe others. AMARU has P_SUS etc. But `P_MSND`/`P_MPAT` aliases absent; can define. `P_FTYPE` present but different position. No issue if compiling in AMARU core: references use symbols. But gen.c writes JIANT-only params like P_POFS? Let's check gen.c for P_ names.

Maybe we should quantify variability:
- AMARU has 9 genre profiles * fixed patterns; drums patterns are 16-char masks with only 4 random conditions. Bass has fixed degree positions. Seed only affects random fills/bpm/root/tone; drums/hats variation chance and lead/pad minimal. So many seeds produce near-identical drum/bass. JIANT uses seed for archetype selection, drum map perturbations, fills, ghost placement, microtiming, etc.
- AMARU's `BASS_ROLL` degree = `(pos*3+bar)&7` capped 4; `BASS_ACID` fixed on positions. Bass root = genre root/scale; pad/lead triads. No chord progression? Wait AMARU `make_pad` uses degrees 0/2/4 and bar variation; no actual chord progression table. JIANT has chord plan with sections and voice leading. This affects bass because bass follows chord roots in JIANT; AMARU bass follows scale degrees, only root. JIANT bass lines are chord-aware, so they sound more musical. That's a key reason.

Need mention AMARU's "FORM" doesn't create sections; JIANT's does. The user says random songs on JIANT; the song-level arrangement is part of it. But they care drum/bass. Still relevant.

Need mention microtiming: user explicitly says "with microtiming etc." JIANT's `ST_MICRO`, swing/human, sd_micro, lane ratchets. AMARU has only a global swing value in genres but does it apply? AMARU's `out->swing = g->swing`; maybe Bunker uses swing? It sets step timing? It has `swing` field but make_drums doesn't use it except output. The generated patterns are grid-locked; no microtiming. JIANT applies microtiming and humanization. This is a reason the groove feels different even with same pattern.

Also JIANT's drum velocity is computed from drum-map level and accents; AMARU uses fixed 88/112 for hits and fixed accents. So dynamics are flat. Another key.

# AMARU OS — Handoff Note

**Date:** 2026-10-26  
**State:** Alpha 0.1a, release-gate *hardware* still pending formal sign-off. Source at commit `17e?` (see `git log`).

## What we shipped today

- **Firmware (AMARU OS)**: derivative of Bunker Evolved 1.0 (GPL-3.0).  
- **Generator (`amaru_gen.c`)**: 9 genres (tribe/mental/hardtekk/acidcore/jungle/dnb/breakbeat/techno/psytrance), 4 tracks (AIR/MELODY/ROOT/SPARK), 3 forms (LOOP/PARTS/SONG). Deterministic seed, GROW/EVOL integration.  
- **Sound recipes**: Carnac/Mycelium-inspired presets (HYPOGEUM CHANT, SKARA HEARTH, SILBURY WAIL, SIBURY MOUND, ORACLE CHOIR, MYC PUNCHY, MYC BLOWN) ported as **numbers** (params), not imported binaries. Plus cosmetic AMARY/MAYA/TUPAC names.  
- **Theme**: strict monochrome palettes GRN/BLK, BLK/WHITE, AMB/BLK; accidental REC red → accent.  
- **Web UI**: AMARU branding; logo splash as 1-bit monochrome bitmap; AMARU 0.1a version.  
- **Web emulator (gh-pages)**: latest `felucca.wasm` deployed; preset alias now returns clean factory names (no PXX staging names).  
- **Sound alias layer (`amaru_sound_alias.c`)**: curated name overlays + fallback to original factory name.  
- **Documentation**: README.md hardware-status & flashing, QUICKSTART, ATTRIBUTION, and release-gate questions answered with test evidence.

## Brick-safety posture today

- Firmware flashes via **Jieli’s stock staging+commit loader**, same as Bunker — a package whose flash size doesn’t match `OTA_FL_LEN` is refused **before** anything is committed.
- Build-system gates pass: `hal/` only register access, single core, RAM .data+.bss 61 KB, flash image 535,612 B.
- **Hardware runtime** (SPL handoff, clock tree, flash write timing) **unverified** — alpha should remain alpha until a formal hardware-test sign-off.

## Future advancements (suggested)

1. **Hardware validation phase**: rehearse V15 rollback, flash one FM-1, confirm no brick, sign off 9-question gate → release **beta**.
2. **Full factory-name catalog** (extend `amaru_sound_alias.c` table beyond 17 curated entries), covering every factory preset of every engine.
3. **Genre-deepening pass**: reduce 16-step text masks to layered pattern generators (sub-step noise + ratchets) for DnB/jungle breaks.
4. **Visual identity pass**: skin `ui_draw.c` track chrome with tiles/leaves (low-level `cv_rect`/`cv_pixel` only, no new engines), e.g. 1-bit vine themes per genre.
5. **Hardware rollback test harness**: drop `scripts/rehearse_rollback.sh` exercising `FELUCCA_ID → newer V15`.
6. **Optional features**: Carnac/Mycelium deep-dive textures (brown-breath `NOISE` layer), psy/swarm timbre model; user-bank cloning tool.

## Attribs maintained

Built on Bunker Evolved 1.0 (Hügelton Instruments), GPL-3.0-only. Engine tools/modules retained. Release-gate doc: `docs/AMARU-ANALYSIS.md`.

# AMARU OS / BUNKER ADVANCED — source analysis and build plan

Status: Step 1 analysis. Baseline imported from Bunker Evolved 1.0 (`c9bb0b1`).
This document is the engineering record for the fusion. It describes what each source
actually does, what will be reused, what will be rebuilt, what will not be imported,
and how the result can be validated without risking the FM-1.

---

## 1. Product definition

**AMARU OS** is the product name of the firmware; **BUNKER ADVANCED** is the
instrument/UI identity inside it.

It is a new FM-1 firmware built on the Bunker Evolved tree, with:

- Bunker Evolved navigation, four tracks, 64-step sequencer, eight shared voices,
  GROW and EVOLVE preserved.
- A deterministic generator with `GENRE`, `SEED`, `ENERGY` and `FORM`
  (`LOOP` / `PARTS` / `SONG`), at least:
  tribe tekno, mental tekno, hardtekk, acidcore, jungle, drum & bass,
  breakbeat tekno, techno, psytrance.
- Genre-specific drum grammar, bass behaviour and arrangement. Jungle, drum & bass
  and breakbeat must not be four-on-the-floor.
- Bunker-native sound recipes for the requested tekno/psy/ambient palette:
  mental pads, tomb drones, sirens, wavetable ghosts, ritual choirs, metal blooms,
  cave pads, psy swarms, acid mists, dark textures, tribe/tekno basses, hardtekk
  stabs, acidcore voices, psy rolling basses/leads, jungle/DnB sub basses and
  breakbeat textures.
- An original monochrome retro-terminal visual layer with three themes:
  green/black, black/white and amber/black.
- No Carnac, Mycelium, JIANT, Bunker, Fallout or Classic Mac binaries/brand assets
  copied in. Character is rebuilt from Bunker's own engines, recipes and drawing
  primitives.

Non-negotiable constraints:

1. Do not brick the FM-1. Keep a tested stock rollback path.
2. Preserve Bunker's workflow. Extend; do not remove functions.
3. Generated material must remain editable by GROW/EVOLVE and by the normal
   step/sound editors.
4. Seed must be deterministic and must survive regeneration.
5. All source licences must remain compatible and attributed.

---

## 2. Sources and provenance

| Source | Local revision | Licence | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bunker Evolved 1.0 | `c9bb0b1` | GPL-3.0-only | Base firmware, UI, sequencer, engines, storage, recovery |
| JIANT tekno fork | `2f16bec` (fork of JIANT `dc8d025` base) | GPL-3.0-only | Genre generator ideas, tekno recipes, tests |
| Carnac OS 0.9.4 | `32369d3` | GPL-3.0 | Wavetable/FX/voice/UI reference; concepts only |
| Mycelium FM-1 1.0 | `750eb12` | GPL-3.0-only | Textures, punch FX, arranger, recovery reference |
| Classic Mac icons | `thomasareed/Classic-Mac-icons` `main` | **No licence found** | **Rejected** (see §7) |

All four firmware sources are GPL-3.0(-only), so a GPL fusion is licence-compatible.
Attribution and licence texts are kept in the repository root and in
`docs/ATTRIBUTION.md`.

Bunker already vendors Felucca-Engines (MIT), msfa (Apache-2.0), CC0 samples and
OFL fonts. Those notices stay with the Bunker tree and must not be removed.

---

## 3. Bunker Evolved — the base

### 3.1 What it is

- Four parts/tracks (`NTRK = NPART = 4`), each with its own engine, preset,
  parameters, eight voices and a 64-step pattern. The eight voices are a shared
  budget.
- 14 engine slots: ANALOG, reserved DIGITAL, PHASE, LOFI, SAMPLE, VOICE/FORMANT,
  TRIO, WHEEL, GRAIN, PHYS, DRUM, NOISE, FM6, SLICE. Engine numbers are store/protocol
  indices and are append-only.
- Four project slots, 114 parameters per project, A/B autosave, song chain,
  GROW/EVOLVE, worlds/sounds/motifs.
- Bunker home pages: `WORLD`, `GROW`, `SOUND`, `MOTIF`, `EVOLVE`, `MIX`, with four
  encoders and OCT+/OCT- actions.
- Existing UI palettes include `GREEN`, `AMBER` and `MONO` (black and white).
  `GREEN` and `AMBER` still use a contrasting accent, so they are not strictly
  monochrome today.

### 3.2 Why it is the base

- It already has the four-track workflow the user wants to keep.
- Its sequencer is the actual audio data model (GROW/EVOLVE edit `step_t`), so a
  generator that writes normal steps is automatically compatible.
- Its storage, bootguard and OTA path are mature and tested.
- Its engines already cover analog, FM6, phase distortion, formant/choir, grain,
  physical modelling, noise, drum synthesis and slicing. That is enough to rebuild
  the Carnac/Mycelium character natively.

### 3.3 Baseline build (verified locally)

Command (one core, as recommended for Bunker):

```sh
python3 firmware/tools/gen_bunker_library.py
cd firmware
JIELI_TOOLCHAIN=/home/user/.jieli/toolchain \
AC79_SDK=/home/user/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK \
FELUCCA_CPU2=0 sh ./build.sh
```

Observed:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| App image | 527,692 B |
| Loader | 6,934 B |
| Package | 610,090 B, identity `FM-1_7100002` |
| RAM `.data + .bss` | 61,156 B of 73,728 B (12,572 B free) |
| Pool | 328,924 B of 368,640 B (39,716 B free) |
| XIP region | `0x8DFBC` = 581,564 B |
| App-image headroom | ≈ 53,872 B |

The exact package headroom depends on the installer/update-loader envelope. Treat
**40 KB of app-image growth as the working ceiling** for AMARU, not 53 KB. RAM and
pool are tighter and must be measured after each milestone.

### 3.4 Storage, update and recovery — what must be preserved

- Updates use the M-UPGRADE SysEx path. The updater checks the UFW header CRCs,
  board flash length (`OTA_FL_LEN = 0x93000`), the update loader, stages the
  loader outside the store area, verifies the staged image by read-back, and only
  commits after the host's explicit success message. A refused package is rejected
  before any erase.
- `bootguard` is RAM-only: two failed boots within the first 30 s fall back to
  UBOOT; it cannot rescue an image that fails before the application starts.
- OCT- + OCT+ held for 5 s enters UBOOT; OCT- alone at power-on enters the
  application-level rescue path (USB installer, audio off).
- Four project slots; autosave may replace old working data. AMB/Wolf projects
  are not migrated. Users must save before installing a different firmware.
- Stock V15 rollback remains the external installer/UBOOT path. AMARU must ship
  with the stock image and checksum documented, and must never erase the
  bootloader.

**Rule for this project:** no hardware flashing until host build, native tests,
emulator boot, update-package verification and a rollback rehearsal are complete.

---

## 4. JIANT tekno fork — generator analysis

### 4.1 What was added by the user

Compared with upstream JIANT base `dc8d025`, the fork changes:

- `firmware/src/gen.c`
- `firmware/src/gen_tables.c`
- `firmware/src/eng_analog.c`
- `firmware/src/ui_draw.c`
- `firmware/src/ui_menu.c`
- `tests/gen_test.c`
- `web/editor.html`

It adds six tekno-family genres in the slots of removed pop/jazz genres, several
new ANALOG presets, and a tekno articulation/envelope pass.

Current genre table (0-based index):

```
26 TRIBE TEKNO   30 BREAKS          31 DRUM & BASS
33 TEKNO         34 MENTAL TEKNO    35 ACID CORE
36 HARDTEKK      42 PSY TRANCE
```

The fork has **no genre named JUNGLE**. Upstream also had no JUNGLE genre; it only
had a `BA_JUNGLE` bass archetype. AMARU must add a first-class JUNGLE profile and a
first-class BREAKBEAT TEKNO profile (BREAKS exists but is not named/parameterised
as breakbeat tekno).

### 4.2 Verified runtime reachability problems

These are real defects in the current fork, not style opinions.

1. **Candidate cap hides the last ANALOG preset.**
   `gen_sound()` collects matching presets into `any[32]`, but
   `ANALOG_PRESETS` now has **33** entries. Index 32 (`MENTAL RING`) is never
   considered. It is one of the newly added tekno presets.
   Consequence: `SR_MENTAL` and `SR_MENTAL_BASS` cannot reach their ANALOG
   `MENTAL RING` branch.

2. **Several recipe words do not exist in the engine the recipe routes to.**
   The selector picks an engine from the recipe's three weighted choices, then
   searches that engine's preset names. If no word matches, it silently falls back
   to any preset. The result still gets the tekno envelope, so the current tests
   pass even though the intended sound was never used.

   | Recipe | Intended words / engines | Broken branches |
   |---|---|---|
   | `SR_ACIDCORE` | CORE 303 / RESO / FM PLUCK, engines A,A,PH | `RESO` not in ANALOG; `FM PLUCK` not in PHASE |
   | `SR_TEKK_BASS` | TEKK BASS / HARD BASS / GROWL, A,A,A | `HARD BASS`, `GROWL` not in ANALOG |
   | `SR_PSY_LEAD` | PSY LEAD / PD LEAD / FM PLUCK, A,A,PH | `PD LEAD` not in ANALOG; `FM PLUCK` not in PHASE |
   | `SR_TEKNO_BASS` | TEKNO BASS / FM BASS / SYN BASS, A,A,A | `FM BASS`, `SYN BASS` not in ANALOG |
   | `SR_MENTAL_BASS` | FM BASS / MENTAL RING / FB BASS, FM,A,PH | ANALOG `MENTAL RING` capped; only FM/PH branches resolve |
   | `SR_MENTAL` | MENTAL SIREN / MENTAL RING / ICE BELL, A,FM,PH | FM `MENTAL RING` missing; PH `ICE BELL` missing |
   | `SR_PSY_BASS` | PSY BASS / REESE / FB BASS, A,A,A | `FB BASS` not in ANALOG |

   `SR_TRIBE_BASS`, `SR_TEKK_STAB`, `SR_TEK_ARP` and `SR_PSY_ARP` resolve
   correctly.

3. **Tests do not catch the above.**
   The new tests check envelope releases, 4/4 kick density and absence of empty
   downbeats. They do not assert that the recipe's named preset was actually
   selected. `GEN_NEVER` does not exclude the new names, and "MENTAL" is not
   accidentally matched by "METAL".

4. **Tests cover only the six tekno genres.** `GG = {27,34,35,36,37,43}` maps to
   `TRIBE TEKNO, TEKNO, MENTAL TEKNO, ACID CORE, HARDTEKK, PSY TRANCE`.
   JUNGLE, DRUM & BASS and BREAKS have no dedicated non-4/4 regression test.

5. **JIANT has six tracks; Bunker has four.** A direct port is impossible without
   changing Bunker's identity, which the brief forbids. The JIANT role model
   (drums, bass, chords/pad, arp, lead, texture) must be compressed to four layers.

### 4.3 Decision for AMARU

- Reuse the **genre concepts, drum/bass grammar, articulation ideas and test

# AMARU OS / BUNKER ADVANCED — source analysis and build plan

Status: Step 1 analysis. Baseline imported from Bunker Evolved 1.0 (`c9bb0b1`).
This document is the engineering record for the fusion. It describes what each source
actually does, what will be reused, what will be rebuilt, what will not be imported,
and how the result can be validated without risking the FM-1.

---

## 1. Product definition

**AMARU OS** is the product name of the firmware; **BUNKER ADVANCED** is the
instrument/UI identity inside it.

It is a new FM-1 firmware built on the Bunker Evolved tree, with:

- Bunker Evolved navigation, four tracks, 64-step sequencer, eight shared voices,
  GROW and EVOLVE preserved.
- A deterministic generator with `GENRE`, `SEED`, `ENERGY` and `FORM`
  (`LOOP` / `PARTS` / `SONG`), at least:
  tribe tekno, mental tekno, hardtekk, acidcore, jungle, drum & bass,
  breakbeat tekno, techno, psytrance.
- Genre-specific drum grammar, bass behaviour and arrangement. Jungle, drum & bass
  and breakbeat must not be four-on-the-floor.
- Bunker-native sound recipes for the requested tekno/psy/ambient palette:
  mental pads, tomb drones, sirens, wavetable ghosts, ritual choirs, metal blooms,
  cave pads, psy swarms, acid mists, dark textures, tribe/tekno basses, hardtekk
  stabs, acidcore voices, psy rolling basses/leads, jungle/DnB sub basses and
  breakbeat textures.
- An original monochrome retro-terminal visual layer with three themes:
  green/black, black/white and amber/black.
- No Carnac, Mycelium, JIANT, Bunker, Fallout or Classic Mac binaries/brand assets
  copied in. Character is rebuilt from Bunker's own engines, recipes and drawing
  primitives.

Non-negotiable constraints:

1. Do not brick the FM-1. Keep a tested stock rollback path.
2. Preserve Bunker's workflow. Extend; do not remove functions.
3. Generated material must remain editable by GROW/EVOLVE and by the normal
   step/sound editors.
4. Seed must be deterministic and must survive regeneration.
5. All source licences must remain compatible and attributed.

---

## 2. Sources and provenance

| Source | Local revision | Licence | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bunker Evolved 1.0 | `c9bb0b1` | GPL-3.0-only | Base firmware, UI, sequencer, engines, storage, recovery |
| JIANT tekno fork | `2f16bec` (fork of JIANT `dc8d025` base) | GPL-3.0-only | Genre generator ideas, tekno recipes, tests |
| Carnac OS 0.9.4 | `32369d3` | GPL-3.0 | Wavetable/FX/voice/UI reference; concepts only |
| Mycelium FM-1 1.0 | `750eb12` | GPL-3.0-only | Textures, punch FX, arranger, recovery reference |
| Classic Mac icons | `thomasareed/Classic-Mac-icons` `main` | **No licence found** | **Rejected** (see §7) |

All four firmware sources are GPL-3.0(-only), so a GPL fusion is licence-compatible.
Attribution and licence texts are kept in the repository root and in
`docs/ATTRIBUTION.md`.

Bunker already vendors Felucca-Engines (MIT), msfa (Apache-2.0), CC0 samples and
OFL fonts. Those notices stay with the Bunker tree and must not be removed.

---

## 3. Bunker Evolved — the base

### 3.1 What it is

- Four parts/tracks (`NTRK = NPART = 4`), each with its own engine, preset,
  parameters, eight voices and a 64-step pattern. The eight voices are a shared
  budget.
- 14 engine slots: ANALOG, reserved DIGITAL, PHASE, LOFI, SAMPLE, VOICE/FORMANT,
  TRIO, WHEEL, GRAIN, PHYS, DRUM, NOISE, FM6, SLICE. Engine numbers are store/protocol
  indices and are append-only.
- Four project slots, 114 parameters per project, A/B autosave, song chain,
  GROW/EVOLVE, worlds/sounds/motifs.
- Bunker home pages: `WORLD`, `GROW`, `SOUND`, `MOTIF`, `EVOLVE`, `MIX`, with four
  encoders and OCT+/OCT- actions.
- Existing UI palettes include `GREEN`, `AMBER` and `MONO` (black and white).
  `GREEN` and `AMBER` still use a contrasting accent, so they are not strictly
  monochrome today.

### 3.2 Why it is the base

- It already has the four-track workflow the user wants to keep.
- Its sequencer is the actual audio data model (GROW/EVOLVE edit `step_t`), so a
  generator that writes normal steps is automatically compatible.
- Its storage, bootguard and OTA path are mature and tested.
- Its engines already cover analog, FM6, phase distortion, formant/choir, grain,
  physical modelling, noise, drum synthesis and slicing. That is enough to rebuild
  the Carnac/Mycelium character natively.

### 3.3 Baseline build (verified locally)

Command (one core, as recommended for Bunker):

```sh
python3 firmware/tools/gen_bunker_library.py
cd firmware
JIELI_TOOLCHAIN=/home/user/.jieli/toolchain \
AC79_SDK=/home/user/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK \
FELUCCA_CPU2=0 sh ./build.sh
```

Observed:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| App image | 527,692 B |
| Loader | 6,934 B |
| Package | 610,090 B, identity `FM-1_7100002` |
| RAM `.data + .bss` | 61,156 B of 73,728 B (12,572 B free) |
| Pool | 328,924 B of 368,640 B (39,716 B free) |
| XIP region | `0x8DFBC` = 581,564 B |
| App-image headroom | ≈ 53,872 B |

The exact package headroom depends on the installer/update-loader envelope. Treat
**40 KB of app-image growth as the working ceiling** for AMARU, not 53 KB. RAM and
pool are tighter and must be measured after each milestone.

### 3.4 Storage, update and recovery — what must be preserved

- Updates use the M-UPGRADE SysEx path. The updater checks the UFW header CRCs,
  board flash length (`OTA_FL_LEN = 0x93000`), the update loader, stages the
  loader outside the store area, verifies the staged image by read-back, and only
  commits after the host's explicit success message. A refused package is rejected
  before any erase.
- `bootguard` is RAM-only: two failed boots within the first 30 s fall back to
  UBOOT; it cannot rescue an image that fails before the application starts.
- OCT- + OCT+ held for 5 s enters UBOOT; OCT- alone at power-on enters the
  application-level rescue path (USB installer, audio off).
- Four project slots; autosave may replace old working data. AMB/Wolf projects
  are not migrated. Users must save before installing a different firmware.
- Stock V15 rollback remains the external installer/UBOOT path. AMARU must ship
  with the stock image and checksum documented, and must never erase the
  bootloader.

**Rule for this project:** no hardware flashing until host build, native tests,
emulator boot, update-package verification and a rollback rehearsal are complete.

---

## 4. JIANT tekno fork — generator analysis

### 4.1 What was added by the user

Compared with upstream JIANT base `dc8d025`, the fork changes:

- `firmware/src/gen.c`
- `firmware/src/gen_tables.c`
- `firmware/src/eng_analog.c`
- `firmware/src/ui_draw.c`
- `firmware/src/ui_menu.c`
- `tests/gen_test.c`
- `web/editor.html`

It adds six tekno-family genres in the slots of removed pop/jazz genres, several
new ANALOG presets, and a tekno articulation/envelope pass.

Current genre table (0-based index):

```
26 TRIBE TEKNO   30 BREAKS          31 DRUM & BASS
33 TEKNO         34 MENTAL TEKNO    35 ACID CORE
36 HARDTEKK      42 PSY TRANCE
```

The fork has **no genre named JUNGLE**. Upstream also had no JUNGLE genre; it only
had a `BA_JUNGLE` bass archetype. AMARU must add a first-class JUNGLE profile and a
first-class BREAKBEAT TEKNO profile (BREAKS exists but is not named/parameterised
as breakbeat tekno).

### 4.2 Verified runtime reachability problems

These are real defects in the current fork, not style opinions.

1. **Candidate cap hides the last ANALOG preset.**
   `gen_sound()` collects matching presets into `any[32]`, but
   `ANALOG_PRESETS` now has **33** entries. Index 32 (`MENTAL RING`) is never
   considered. It is one of the newly added tekno presets.
   Consequence: `SR_MENTAL` and `SR_MENTAL_BASS` cannot reach their ANALOG
   `MENTAL RING` branch.

2. **Several recipe words do not exist in the engine the recipe routes to.**
   The selector picks an engine from the recipe's three weighted choices, then
   searches that engine's preset names. If no word matches, it silently falls back
   to any preset. The result still gets the tekno envelope, so the current tests
   pass even though the intended sound was never used.

   | Recipe | Intended words / engines | Broken branches |
   |---|---|---|
   | `SR_ACIDCORE` | CORE 303 / RESO / FM PLUCK, engines A,A,PH | `RESO` not in ANALOG; `FM PLUCK` not in PHASE |
   | `SR_TEKK_BASS` | TEKK BASS / HARD BASS / GROWL, A,A,A | `HARD BASS`, `GROWL` not in ANALOG |
   | `SR_PSY_LEAD` | PSY LEAD / PD LEAD / FM PLUCK, A,A,PH | `PD LEAD` not in ANALOG; `FM PLUCK` not in PHASE |
   | `SR_TEKNO_BASS` | TEKNO BASS / FM BASS / SYN BASS, A,A,A | `FM BASS`, `SYN BASS` not in ANALOG |
   | `SR_MENTAL_BASS` | FM BASS / MENTAL RING / FB BASS, FM,A,PH | ANALOG `MENTAL RING` capped; only FM/PH branches resolve |
   | `SR_MENTAL` | MENTAL SIREN / MENTAL RING / ICE BELL, A,FM,PH | FM `MENTAL RING` missing; PH `ICE BELL` missing |
   | `SR_PSY_BASS` | PSY BASS / REESE / FB BASS, A,A,A | `FB BASS` not in ANALOG |

   `SR_TRIBE_BASS`, `SR_TEKK_STAB`, `SR_TEK_ARP` and `SR_PSY_ARP` resolve
   correctly.

3. **Tests do not catch the above.**
   The new tests check envelope releases, 4/4 kick density and absence of empty
   downbeats. They do not assert that the recipe's named preset was actually
   selected. `GEN_NEVER` does not exclude the new names, and "MENTAL" is not
   accidentally matched by "METAL".

4. **Tests cover only the six tekno genres.** `GG = {27,34,35,36,37,43}` maps to
   `TRIBE TEKNO, TEKNO, MENTAL TEKNO, ACID CORE, HARDTEKK, PSY TRANCE`.
   JUNGLE, DRUM & BASS and BREAKS have no dedicated non-4/4 regression test.

5. **JIANT has six tracks; Bunker has four.** A direct port is impossible without
   changing Bunker's identity, which the brief forbids. The JIANT role model
   (drums, bass, chords/pad, arp, lead, texture) must be compressed to four layers.

### 4.3 Decision for AMARU

- Reuse the **genre concepts, drum/bass grammar, articulation ideas and test

state.output:
# Tekno generator core

This note covers the second pass over the six tekno-family rows (TRIBE TEKNO, TEKNO, MENTAL TEKNO, ACID CORE,
HARDTEKK, PSY TRANCE). The first patch replaced six genre slots and added recipes, presets, drum maps and bass
archetypes. That made the genre names appear, but several musical decisions were still being overwritten after the
fact. This pass makes the dedicated material survive the generator and adds a small, deterministic articulation layer.

## Scope and safety

The change is generator-only:

- `firmware/src/gen_tables.c`: recipe-envelope helper, six genre rows, one acoustic-core recipe swap.
- `firmware/src/gen.c`: final-envelope policy, recipe throw policy, tekno bass articulation pass.
- `tests/gen_test.c`: genre-aware regression tests.
- Documentation only elsewhere.

No bootloader, OTA/update path, recovery path, partition table, flash layout, storage format or project format was
touched. The host emulator path still boots and renders (`web/emu/native_check.c`). See **Validation** for the exact
host checks and the one limitation: no JieLi toolchain/SDK is available in this workspace, so a full firmware image
was not built here.

## What was wrong

Measured over eight seeds per genre before the change:

| Genre | bass release | kick / bass mode | bass slides (8 seeds) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TRIBE TEKNO | 40..40 | ANSWER | 16 |
| TEKNO | 40..40 | SUSTAIN | 28 |
| MENTAL TEKNO | 0..40 | SUSTAIN | 36 |
| ACID CORE | 40..40 | SUSTAIN | 33 |
| HARDTEKK | 40..43 | SUSTAIN | **0** |
| PSY TRANCE | 40..40 | SUSTAIN | **0** |

The ACID CORE bass recipe asks for a 18..32 release, but `gen_sound()` clamped every role to `GREL[role][0]` (40 for
bass). Dedicated lead/arp recipes were then overwritten by the generic lead/arp envelope shapes. The six rows also
shared essentially one kick/bass mode, and two bass archetypes never produced a slide.

## Envelope policy

`gtekno_voice(ri)` names the dedicated tekno recipes. For those recipes:

- the generic lead/arp ADSR shape is skipped;
- the final release floor is **24**, not the role floor (still inside `GREL[role][1]`).

Twenty-four is short enough to preserve a 303 / tekk gesture and long enough to stay clear of a click at the genre
tempos. Everything else keeps the existing role policy. `gtekno_genre(gi)` identifies the six rows, and the
neighbour-recipe throw (`SR_ALT`) is skipped for them, so a TRIBE throw cannot replace its tribe bass with a rock
bass and silently invalidate the envelope agreement. EXPLORE and mutant pieces still use the old throw rules.

Final measured releases after the change (non-FM6 tracks):

| Genre | final bass release | final lead | final arp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TRIBE TEKNO | 24..26 | 45..68 | 24..35 |
| TEKNO | 24..30 | 40..69 | 24..33 |
| MENTAL TEKNO | 24..28 | 43..70 | 41..64 |
| ACID CORE | 24..32 | 24..31 | 24..35 |
| HARDTEKK | 24..26 | 35..58 | 24..35 |
| PSY TRANCE | 24..35 | 41..59 | 31..31 |

FM6 uses the carriers' R4 for its release (`fm6_rel_r4`); those tracks are excluded from the release assertion rather
than forced onto a value the engine does not use.

## Articulation pass

`gtekno_artic()` runs at the end of `gen_post()` for the six genres only (not EXPLORE, not mutants). It uses its own
deterministic PRNG seeded from the piece, so it does not move the shared generator stream or another part's gestures.

- If the bass has no slides, it adds one or two hinges into a following note, skipping ties. It usually avoids the
  downbeat so the kick keeps its weight.
- If the bass has fewer than two accents, it adds offbeat accents, never on a quarter.
- MENTAL TEKNO may hold one phrase tail into a following rest, but never over a chord change or a kick.

Measured after the change: 2267 bass notes, 468 accents, 140 slides across 48 pieces. Every piece has at least two
accents and one slide. Before the pass HARDTEKK and PSY had zero slides.

This is deliberately a grammar, not a fixed pattern: it only fills a missing gesture and leaves existing accents and
slides alone.

## Kick / bass handovers

The six rows now use four distinct modes:

| Genre | Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| TRIBE TEKNO | `KM_INTERLOCK` | the bass answers the step after the kick |
| TEKNO | `KM_DOUBLE` | the bass doubles the kick when it rests |
| MENTAL TEKNO | `KM_SUSTAIN` | the bass sustains through the kick, ducked |
| ACID CORE | `KM_ANSWER` | the bass stops on the kick's step |
| HARDTEKK | `KM_DOUBLE` | hard doubling against the kick |
| PSY TRANCE | `KM_SUSTAIN` | rolling sustained bass under the kick |

ACID CORE's arp recipe moved from `SR_ACIDCORE` to `SR_TEK_ARP`; the bass and lead still use the dedicated 303
recipe, but the third acid layer no longer stacks the same envelope a third time.

The regression test requires four distinct modes, no empty downbeat, at least 87 % of quarters on each row (ACID
CORE's last-bar fill and TRIBE TEKNO's half-time throw are the deliberate holes) and at least 94 % over all 48
pieces. The holes are not smoothed away.

## Determinism and rollback

- Same settings still produce the same piece. The articulation stream is local and seeded from `gp.seed`, `gi` and a
  fixed salt.
- No new global random draws were inserted into the shared streams except the already existing recipe throw draw,
  which is still consumed but ignored for the six rows.
- To roll back, revert the three source files (`gen_tables.c`, `gen.c`, `gen_test.c`) and this note. There is no
  migration, stored-format change or one-way action.
- Existing non-tekno genres keep their old code paths.

## Validation

Host tests (this workspace):

```sh
mkdir -p build/gen build/host build/emu
# generate the headers into build/gen as documented in tests/gen_test.c
cc -O1 -w -Ibuild/gen -Ifirmware/src -Itests -o build/host/gen_test tests/gen_test.c -lm
./build/host/gen_test
```

Result: `gen: all passed` (72 checks).

Host emulator boot/render:

```sh
cc -O2 -ffp-contract=off -w -Ibuild/gen -Ifirmware/src -o build/emu/native_check web/emu/native_check.c -lm
./build/emu/native_check /tmp/after.f32
```

Result: boots, renders 176400 float samples, peak 0.271, RMS 0.058; no clipping. This exercises the firmware sources
through the emulator's host path, but it is not a hardware test.

Not verified here:

- a full FM-1 firmware image (no JieLi toolchain / AC79 SDK in the workspace);
- listening tests, matched-loudness A/B, or hardware voice-count/timing checks;
- on-device flash/update behaviour (intentionally out of scope).

Run `tests/run_tests.sh` in an environment with the firmware build artefacts before publishing a release image.

## Design notes

The intent is a role and relationship, not a mandatory pattern: a kick/bass handover, a small accent/slide vocabulary,
and a recipe that owns its envelope. More notes are not the goal. The next useful step is an audition pass at matched
loudness on hardware, followed by a preset-reachability check for the named tekno voices if the preset bank changes.
